h1: Zomato introduces plastics-free food packaging across their restaurant network
h2: Zomato introduces plastics-free food packaging across their restaurant network
h4: A first-of-its-kind rollout of PFAs-free, plastic-free coated-paper packaging across one of India’s largest food-delivery supply chains.
p: Zomato is one of India’s largest food-delivery and HoReCa platforms, connecting millions of consumers with more than 247,000 restaurant partners nationwide. Hyperpure, its B2B supplies vertical, provides packaging and essentials to 30,000+ restaurants across major Indian cities. With the rapid expansion of takeaway and delivery, Zomato–Hyperpure needed a high-performance, regulation-aligned packaging alternative that eliminated synthetic coatings and hidden plastics without disrupting food safety or operational throughput.

Large parts of the restaurant ecosystem still relied on food boxes, trays, and containers made from paper coated with synthetic plastics or fossil-based materials. These coatings delivered necessary grease and moisture resistance but introduced PFAs, microplastics, and compliance risks. Hyperpure lacked a commercially ready, scalable solution that was plastic-free, PFAs-free, and capable of supporting hot foods, durability, and barrier performance at the scale required by India’s food-service market.

Zerocircle supplied coated-paper food boxes, trays, and containers — available in white and kraft variants — engineered without fossil-based coatings, plastic liners, or PFAs. These products deliver functional barrier performance required for hot, oily, and moisture-heavy foods, while meeting emerging regulatory expectations. By integrating these SKUs into its portfolio, Hyperpure became one of India’s first major food-service networks to move core single-use packaging categories into genuinely plastic-free materials.
A first-of-its-kind rollout of PFAs-free, plastic-free coated-paper packaging across one of India’s largest food-delivery supply chains.

Initial commercialisation: 100,000 coated-paper food boxes, trays, and containers supplied through Hyperpure’s distribution network.

Scale trajectory: Further orders under discussion, with plans for wider deployment across cities, restaurant partners, and cuisine formats.

Product focus: Zerocircle’s coated-paper technology for high-volume food-service packaging.
Plastic diversion: Each coated-paper unit replaces a fossil-based or synthetic-lined container, reducing hidden plastics entering landfill and marine litter streams.
Regulatory leadership: All products are PFAs-free, synthetic-coating-free, and aligned with circular-material and emerging SUPD-inspired frameworks.
System-ready integration: The materials run on standard converting lines, enabling frictionless adoption across Hyperpure’s supply chain.
Socio-economic value: Scaling seaweed-derived coatings strengthens coastal livelihoods and decreases dependence on fossil-derived materials.
Sector leadership: Zomato / Hyperpure set a precedent for India’s food-delivery platforms by mainstreaming truly sustainable, performance-ready packaging.

h1: Eco-Dispo & Zerocircle scale PFAs-free food packaging across Netherlands
h2: Eco-Dispo & Zerocircle scale PFAs-free food packaging across Netherlands
h4: The first commercial rollout of seaweed-based coated packaging in The Netherlands — built for EU compliance, ready for scale, and designed for modern foodservice performance.

Zerocircle fits seamlessly into this value chain. Their seaweed-based coating technology allowed us to significantly strengthen and upgrade our assortment without compromising on performance or usability. Together, we were able to introduce packaging solutions that go beyond existing PLA or PE coatings, offering a natural and circular alternative that aligns with both regulatory developments and market demand.
p: Eco-Dispo is a Netherlands-based distributor known for accelerating sustainable foodservice packaging adoption across the Benelux region. After introducing agave-based straws to Europe, the company built strong channels with cafés, restaurant chains, and global food brands seeking high-performance, microplastic-free solutions that comply with stringent EU sustainability regulations.

As EU demand surged for materials free from microplastics, PFAs, and fossil-derived coatings, Eco-Dispo sought to expand beyond straws into premium takeaway packaging. Existing European options often required trade-offs — weaker barrier performance, steep price premiums, or limited scalability. Eco-Dispo needed a packaging solution that met EU SUPD compliance/exemption criteria, REACH standards, and PFAs-free requirements, while remaining cost-competitive and ready for mass distribution.

Zerocircle partnered with Eco-Dispo to introduce seaweed-coated food boxes — in both white and kraft variants — tailored for restaurants, cafés, and food brands across The Netherlands and the wider Benelux region. The coatings deliver strong oil and moisture resistance without fossil-derived or toxic additives, ensuring alignment with EU regulatory expectations. Because the coated board runs on standard converting and printing lines, distributors and food brands can transition without operational changes.
The first commercial rollout of seaweed-based coated packaging in The Netherlands — built for EU compliance, ready for scale, and designed for modern foodservice performance.

Commercial rollout (2025): Eco-Dispo began distributing Zerocircle’s coated food boxes across its network — marking The Netherlands’ first large-scale deployment of seaweed-based packaging.

1.5 million units sold (as of 2025).

Target: Replace 2 million boxes by March 2026.

Formats: White and kraft coated paperboard to support brand differentiation, print requirements, and varied food applications.

The pilot showed strong uptake from foodservice brands seeking reliable, regulation-aligned packaging that delivers consistent barrier performance without plastic or PFAs.
Plastic displacement: 1.2m units of plastic-coated packaging replaced across Eco-Dispo’s network.
Reduced ocean-litter risk: Each tonne of seaweed-coated board replaces plastic-coated materials that commonly leak into landfill or marine waste streams.
Economic and social value: Seaweed cultivation and processing strengthen coastal livelihoods across India and Southeast Asia, supporting diversified, ocean-positive income sources.
System integration: Zerocircle’s coated board runs smoothly on existing converting lines and integrates effortlessly into Eco-Dispo’s distribution channels.

h1: Schmancy partners with Zerocircle to lead shift towards algae-based coatings
h2: Schmancy partners with Zerocircle to lead shift towards algae-based coatings
h4: A seamless shift from plastic-coated paperboard to a PFAs-free, microplastic-free seaweed coating — without any change to Schmancy’s existing converting infrastructure.

“Working with Zerocircle has been collaborative and solution-oriented. The team is responsive, technically sound, and open to iteration, which makes them feel more like a long-term partner than just a supplier.”
p: Schmancy Pack Pvt. Ltd. is one of India’s leading packaging converters, known for its design-forward, sustainability-driven solutions for cafés, bakeries, restaurants, and lifestyle brands. As demand accelerates for safe, microplastic-free packaging, Schmancy has been actively transitioning its portfolio toward next-generation materials that meet global compliance standards without compromising performance.

Schmancy’s coated-paper packaging line depended on conventional plastic or synthetic coatings to deliver moisture and grease resistance. While effective, these coatings created a growing set of challenges: they made packaging non-compostable, introduced PFAs and microplastic concerns, and placed Schmancy under increasing regulatory and customer pressure to shift away from fossil-derived materials. The company needed a high-performance alternative that could replace plastic coatings without disrupting quality, printability, or production throughput.

Zerocircle partnered with Schmancy to integrate its seaweed-based coated paperboard — a marine-safe, home-compostable, PFAs-free barrier designed for seamless use on existing converting lines. The material matches the barrier performance of traditional plastic coatings, ensuring durability, food safety, and shelf-life integrity. Zerocircle initiated the partnership with a 100 kg pilot batch, converted into food boxes and trays for early customer validation. A 100 kg batch typically yields 2,500–3,000 medium-sized boxes depending on GSM and dimensions.
A seamless shift from plastic-coated paperboard to a PFAs-free, microplastic-free seaweed coating — without any change to Schmancy’s existing converting infrastructure.

The pilot demonstrated strong converting performance and commercial readiness. Both teams are now scaling toward replacing at least 5 tons of plastic-coated paperboard per month, creating a clear pathway for Schmancy to transition its broader food packaging portfolio to seaweed-based alternatives.
Plastic displacement: Replacing 5 tons of plastic-coated paperboard monthly removes hidden plastics and PFAs from Schmancy’s packaging line.
Circular design: Zerocircle’s coatings run on existing equipment with no new capex or line modifications.
Regulatory alignment: Materials are PFAs-free, microplastic-free, REACH-safe, and SUPD-aligned.
Economic and social value: Seaweed cultivation supports coastal farming communities across India and Southeast Asia.
Brand advantage: Enhances Schmancy’s positioning as a converter delivering premium, compliant, next-generation packaging for global brands.

h1: Designing microplastic-free food packaging for Peakst8
h2: Designing microplastic-free food packaging for Peakst8
h4: Every snack at Peakst8 was served in packaging designed with the same intention as the workouts — clean, high-performance, and built for long-term health.
p: Peakst8 Festival is a one-day fitness and wellness celebration bringing together runners, strength athletes, coaches, founders, and health-first brands. Held on 10 January 2026 at the Centre for Sports Excellence, the event hosted over 3,000 participants across workouts, challenges, recovery sessions, and panels. With performance and long-term health at its core, Peakst8 partnered with Zerocircle to ensure that even food packaging aligned with the same standard of care.

Large-scale consumer events generate high volumes of single-use food packaging, particularly for fast-moving snack stalls. Conventional paper boxes are often lined with plastic coatings that shed microplastics and persist in landfill, drains, or incineration streams. For an event focused on movement, recovery, and health, this disconnect between values and materials was impossible to ignore. The organisers needed packaging that could handle volume, food performance, and brand intent — without hidden plastics.

Zerocircle was appointed as the official snack-box partner for Peakst8, supplying high-performance, microplastic-free food boxes across curated food stalls including Two Brothers, Hello Tempayy, Traye, and The Health Factory. The boxes delivered strong oil and moisture resistance for hot, protein-rich foods while remaining plastic-free and compostable. Standardised packaging ensured consistency across vendors while supporting fast service throughout the day.
Every snack at Peakst8 was served in packaging designed with the same intention as the workouts — clean, high-performance, and built for long-term health.

The deployment supported continuous food service across a full-day festival with more than 3,000 attendees and multiple food partners. Scalable stock planning and seamless integration allowed vendors to operate at peak speed without compromising hygiene, food quality, or brand experience — demonstrating readiness for large, complex public events.
Operational reliability: Snack boxes performed consistently across vendors with no disruption to service speed or food integrity.
Health-aligned storytelling: Packaging reinforced the idea that health extends beyond nutrition and movement to the materials that touch food.
High-intent brand exposure: Zerocircle’s materials were present in the hands of thousands of fitness-first consumers and leading health brands throughout the event.
Event-scale validation: Proved that microplastic-free packaging can support high-volume festivals without reverting to plastic-lined alternatives.

h1: How Swiggy tested microplastic-free packaging across 30 burger destinations
h2: How Swiggy tested microplastic-free packaging across 30 burger destinations
h4: A cultural food moment became a systems-level test — and proof — that plastic-free packaging can work at delivery scale.
p: Swiggy is India’s leading on-demand food and convenience platform, shaping how millions of urban consumers eat every day. Burgers are among the most ordered items on the platform and a core part of modern comfort food culture. For International Burger Day, Swiggy set out to transform its flagship #IndiasCoolestBurgers campaign into more than a celebration of taste — using it as a live demonstration of how climate-forward packaging can work at real delivery scale.

Most burgers are delivered in plastic-lined paper boxes that persist long after the meal is finished, accumulating in landfills, drains, and incineration streams. These materials introduce microplastics into ecosystems while remaining invisible to consumers. Swiggy wanted to replace these boxes with packaging that was genuinely microplastic-free and safe for waterways, without compromising the food experience or asking restaurants to change how they operate.

Zerocircle partnered with Swiggy to launch a special-edition seaweed-coated burger box for the #IndiasCoolestBurgers campaign. The boxes were engineered to be microplastic-free, greaseproof, leak-proof, and compatible with existing restaurant workflows. On International Burger Day, Swiggy rolled out these boxes as a one-for-one replacement for conventional plastic-lined containers — proving that sustainable packaging can perform under demanding, real-world delivery conditions.
A cultural food moment became a systems-level test — and proof — that plastic-free packaging can work at delivery scale.

30,000 seaweed-coated burger boxes supplied free of cost to restaurant partners in the first phase.
Deployment across 30 high-volume burger destinations in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Noida, Gurgaon, and Faridabad.
No operational changes required for restaurant kitchens or delivery workflows.
The rollout demonstrated that drop-in, microplastic-free packaging can scale across dense cities, long delivery radii, and high-order volumes.
Plastic avoidance: 30,000 plastic-lined burger boxes eliminated in a single campaign phase.
Restaurant-ready adoption: Cult burger brands and cloud kitchens transitioned seamlessly without changing equipment or processes.
Brand leadership: Swiggy embedded sustainability into one of its most emotional, high-visibility food moments rather than isolating it as a side initiative.
Performance validation: Zerocircle’s seaweed-based barrier coatings matched the demands of greasy, high-moisture foods across long delivery distances.

h2: Building new materialsand breaking old barriers
h4: Building new materialsand breaking old barriers
Our materials
p: Does convenience always have to come at a cost to the planet? Or can everyday things, that have become second nature to us, simply come from nature?

We fell in love with rapidly renewing biomass, at first sight. Through low-energy processes that preserve their inherent advantages we transform natural polymers into materials that run on existing lines and maintain stable performance.

Natural polymers demand chemistry that enhances their strengths while respecting their limits. By avoiding synthetic additives and working with their native structure, we deliver stable performance and a clean, predictable end-of-life.

We work around the  distinct properties of natural compounds, with simple processing, predictable flow and minimal adjustments. By staying within the existing rhythm of production, our materials scale without friction.

Our relationship with natural polymers is built on mutual respect. They don’t overstay their welcome, and we don’t hold them back. As we begin to unlock nature’s potential, packaging becomes just the first chapter in building a plastic-free portfolio across industries.

/vision.title: Vision | We don't want a lasting impression
/vision.description: The one way we want you to remember Zerocircle products is how quickly you can forget about them.
h2: We don’t want a lasting impression
The one way we want you to remember Zerocircle products is how quickly you can forget about them.
h4: We don’t want a lasting impression
The one way we want you to remember Zerocircle products is how quickly you can forget about them.
Neha Jain
p: One year into my attempt at a low carbon footprint lifestyle, I realized that emissions occurring at an industrial scale cannot be significantly reduced by individual choices. And what choices do we really have? Even a single blade of the hardiest grass uses freshwater, a fast depleting, finite resource. How could my attempt rewire something as fundamental as that? Instead of shunning industry, the answer is to find an alternative building block that future industries could switch to.Ironically, the answer lies in the industry's greatest dumpyard - the ocean. The many varieties of seaweed that grow in the ocean contain vast reserves of nutrients that can be used to mitigate food scarcity, birth sustainable packaging, reverse climate change and do so much more.With Zerocircle, I intend to use seaweed to create bio-alternatives to products that we use in our daily lives and enable organisations to create solutions that are perfectly circular, and leave nothing behind. And make a zero waste lifestyle as easy as instant noodles.
Our optimism isn’t blind hope, it’s a deep unshaken belief in humanity's ability to fix what’s broken with science & technology.
We’re driven by possibility, rather than perfection. Our shared trust that a better solution and a bigger challenge is always around the corner is what pushes us to do more.

We don’t chase ideas for the sake of innovation. We build solutions that can be manufactured, shipped and used at scale. If it can’t run on a production line or move through the world, it isn’t ready.
We’re not neutral in this story. We stand against waste, against greenwashing and against delay. Building better materials is not a choice we made, but simply a duty we acted on.
We believe that clarity builds trust and rather than hide behind complexity, communicate the science with intent. Because good ideas need to be understood, not decoded.

Why Zerocircle?

We first came across Zerocircle after they won the Tom Ford Plastic Innovation Prize, which immediately sparked our interest. At Eco-Dispo, we are constantly searching for partners who are not only innovative on paper, but who genuinely challenge the status quo in sustainability.

As India’s leading food delivery platform, we see how deeply burgers shape urban food culture. With Zerocircle, we’re asking a timely question: can our favourite bites be more sustainable? This collaboration celebrates the country’s top burger destinations, and empowers them to serve smarter with packaging that returns safely to nature.

Zerocircle’s materials integrate seamlessly into our packaging development process, allowing us to offer eco-friendly alternatives to our clients without disrupting manufacturing workflows. This makes it easier for us to transition customers toward sustainable packaging while maintaining quality, usability, and cost viability.

In short: Zerocircle is our most trusted partner. The collaboration has been nothing short of exceptional. From jointly entering the Benelux market to developing new products, Zerocircle truly works with us, not just as a regular supplier. They actively think along, leave room for our own ideas, and approach the partnership as a shared journey rather than a transaction.

We were looking for genuinely sustainable materials that could replace conventional plastic without compromising on performance or scalability. Zerocircle stood out because of its clear material science approach, transparency, and focus on real-world applications rather than just sustainability claims.
p: We’ve enabled conscious brands to go plastic free, without risks or asterisks.
From everyday packaging to demanding formats, our materials have stepped in where plastic once did, without compromising performance.

Active engagements across brands and manufacturers

At Peakst8 Festival, every detail — including food packaging — was designed around health and performance. Zerocircle supplied microplastic-free snack boxes for 3,000+ participants across a high-energy, multi-vendor fitness event.

Eco-Dispo partnered with Zerocircle to bring seaweed-coated, PFAs-free takeaway boxes to the European foodservice market. With 1.5 million units already sold and a target of 2 million by 2026, the collaboration marks the first commercial rollout of seaweed-based packaging in The Netherlands.

For International Burger Day, Swiggy partnered with Zerocircle to replace plastic-lined burger boxes with microplastic-free, seaweed-coated packaging. Rolled out across 30 top burger destinations and 30,000 orders, the campaign proved that sustainable packaging can perform at India’s delivery scale.
From pilot to full-scale transition, Schmancy has moved its food packaging line onto seaweed-based coatings. A new benchmark for plastic-free, regulation-ready converting is taking shape.

Zomato–Hyperpure partnered with Zerocircle to introduce PFAs-free, plastic-free coated-paper packaging across its restaurant network.This marks one of the first large-scale shifts to truly microplastic-free packaging in India’s food-delivery ecosystem.

For companies ready to move beyond greenwashing and make tangible, measurable change. Zerocircle is the bridge between ambition and action that helps you replace harmful materials with circular alternatives without sacrificing form or function.

You’ll receive ocean-safe materials designed to return to nature, not landfills. From design to production, we collaborate closely, offering prototyping, transparency, and guidance — a partnership rooted in regeneration.

Because Zerocircle materials integrate seamlessly into existing systems and machinery, adopting sustainability doesn’t require starting over. Our solutions are designed for effortless transition — enabling brands to shift to regenerative materials without disrupting production or performance.
